This is the spot the robot mentioned, where he was supposed to mount your head, after defeating you, as a trophy on display for Rex,
right in front of the funhouse-of-a-dungeon that dork Benny Zinkland made.
According to the robot, somewhere nearby is the secret way out of this mini-realm of fun and games.
Rex is supposed to come by at some point and open it, preparing for Benny Zinkland to come and taunt you, but only when your head
is all that's left of you and is mounted on the fence for him to mock and laugh at.
Do you want to pull a trick on Rex and Benny by putting your head here, while the rest of you hides with your friends nearby?
You can't put your head here because you don't have it with you.  Did you lose it?
You can't put your head here while its still attached.
You're currently wearing it on top of your neck.
You lift up your severed head and put it on a sharp protruding spike coming off of the wood.  The whole fence has these spikes, probably
Your head speaks up: "Hey, good idea, I can gather some intel while you and the others hide, and you can fetch me later."
Your head starts to slide down a little, so you re-center the bottom of it on the spike and push down a little, slightly impaling
it on the spike so it stays put.
Your head talks:  "Yeah yeah, go ahead and impale me, come on, don't be shy...  I don't wanna fall off.  It's not like it hurts of course..."
"Shit \P[1], don't be so careful about it, what are you afraid of?"
You shrug and push your head all the way down on the spike, as far as it will go, until you're certain the spike is pushing against the
top inside of your head's skull.  Being a half-dragon, and playing with swords when you were little, you've been through this sort of
thing before in the backyard when playing games with friends and neighbors, and you know for a fact that this doesn't hurt or kill
your head.  With your half-dragon magic, it simply works.
Your head talks: "Bingo!  All right, that should keep me from falling off!  Okay, you can go hide now if you can find a spot,
though there aren't many good hiding places that I can see here.  Maybe you should go to the Inn or something and come back later."
You're not too worried about your head.  Your instincts and reflexes suppress things when you're decapitated, like an itch on your
nose and other stuff that might bug you if your head were attached.
Worst case scenario, if something really is bugging your face, you feel your sense of touch, smell, and taste from your head and face just
the same, even though it isn't attached, and your head still feels your body and what you do with it.  You would know if something or someone
came and did something to your head.
A little bit of blood from your head trickles down the fence as you step away, planning on returning later.
You see your decapitated head, impaled and mounted on the fence, right where you left it.
Your eyes turn and look at your body as it walks up and stands in front of it.
"Hi \P[1], I haven't seen Rex or Benny Zinkland yet.  Yeah, I'm still alive, I'm fine.  Just bored.  No insects or vermin came,
smelling my blood, and started eating me yet."
"You'll just have to come back later, and do without me for now."
You stand there for a minute, frustrated.
"\P[1], I'm telling ya, go have fun or something.  Go fight a few battles to kill some time, then relax at the Inn!
Don't hang around here and mess anything up in case Benny or Rex come by."
You shrug and turn away, planning to come back later.
You see your decapitated head, impaled and mounted on the fence, right where you left it.
You notice that new stuff is written on the sign next to your head.
Your head notices you approach, and perks up a little.
"Dude!  Been a while!  Yeah your head is still alive.  Man do I have a lot to tell you.  Just know ya can't re-attach me and resync memories,
'cuz Benny Zinkland didn't want me to bleed all over the fence, so he had his goons cauterize your head's underside to make the bleeding stop.
Yeah, I saw him while you were gone, and he wanted your head kept alive, so that it would last forever according to his ideas, and he could
keep it on this fence as his number-one prized trophy."
"He's mental or something!  Man, he's got some serious metal in his microwave!  He thinks the rest of me is dead, the rest of you guys too,
and he wants to bully and taunt me all day long for many YEARS with me on this fence the whole time, where he gets to poke fun at me, pee
on my face when he goes by, and still envy my pretty face with it's perfect skin and beautiful freckles or whatever, all jealous as fuck
"But hey, I gotta tell you more later, so don't kill your head and grow a new one yet.  We need to talk, but not here.  He might be
back any time, him or his sidekick, Rex, that monster he created that he has in charge of this place."
"Don't leave me here either, whether you kill your head or not, 'cuz he's gonna find out sometime anyways the rest of me is running
around still alive, and he might kill your head but then you won't get me to tell the rest of me what I saw including how to get out
of this place.  We gotta move, and NOW."
You pull your head off of the spike that is part of the fence.  It would be nice if you could reattach it now, but you know
that won't work, not with that stupid cauterized flesh the exposed bottom of your head now has.  There's just no way it would
connect to your neck now.  At least you got it back and its still alive, and safe in your hands.
Your head was impaled pretty far onto that spike, just like how you left it.  That spike went deep into the inside of your skull,
and it probably really did run into the bottom inside surface of the top of your skull's bone tissue.  Some of the 'sponge' - as
it is called, referring to the tissue inside your skull where pure humans have brain tissue - comes out and is left on the spike.
Nothing new, you'd be surprised if it didn't do that.
Your sponge, by the way, is not your brain tissue.  You actually have sponge in parts of your torso and body too, and although there are
different types in your half-dragon magical anatomy, the type inside your head is just 'filler' as it doesn't really do anything other than
buffer and hold blood and give your head weight so that it weighs close to what a human head weighs.  If some of it comes out of your head
or even gets carved out like a pumpkin, you don't care - you don't actually need it and losing it won't really hurt you.
As for where your actual brains are, you have multiple brains in 'extradimensional space' - kinda like how the Inn is tiny on
the outside but huge on the inside, you have large amounts of half-dragon anatomy in a custom other dimension, so that in
standard, regular 3D space your body parts don't need to take up much room.  This allows your body parts in standard space to
be so skinny, making you super-slender compared to pure humans, who by comparison have much more bulk.
This is related to how your head and body both live when you are dismembered, decapitated, etc.  All your body parts are connected to
internal anatomy in extradimensional space, including nerves and blood vessels, etc., which is how your severed head can still breath
air and work your body's lungs and not push air in and out of a hole of the severed flesh at the bottom of your head right now.  The
back of your throat goes to a windpipe and esophagus that go from your throat into extradimensional territory.
This goes to your lungs and digestive tract in extradimensional space, and other tissues there which your torso is connected
to.  That's how your head can eat food and it doesn't fall out the bottom of it when it is decapitated, but instead goes to your
stomach and from your headless body you feel it, and maintain a shared blood supply with your head, as well as nerves, hormones,
the works.  Meanwhile, your neck and torso flex and move and change shape consistent with breathing, etc., as if you had lungs...
...inside of your torso, which you actually don't.  If someone looks at a cross-section of your torso cut in half through, say, the
waist - something that's happened before when you practice swordfighting and get cut in half - You don't have any digestive tract or
lungs in standard space, all you have inside your skinny torso is filler tissue, sponge.
Let's just say that your half-dragon anatomy is naturally grown and 'built' to handle being cut apart with grace and keep going.
"Dude.  Thanks \P[1], I've been bored as fuck being here all night.  And after Benny pissing all over me, man, it hasn't been too much fun."
"OK, let's get outta here.  Chit-chat with me later, and I'll tell you what went on, 'cuz we can't re-sync memories the usual way."
Your severed head, as usual, is in your shared inventory, under 'Key Items.'  You can USE it like other inventory items to talk to it,
any time it isn't on your neck, in case you haven't already figured that out by now.
Normally your head only knows what the rest of you knows, but sometimes, for example if you leave it sitting around to spy on people while
playing dead, then get it back later, your head will know what it saw and heard while you were gone, including talking to people when it
The usual way to get whatever intel it gathered when you do this is to just simply re-attach it, which re-syncs your multiple minds and
their memories, and then you have two sets of memories you can think back through for the whole time you were decapitated, one from the
point of view of being in your headless body, and the other from being in your severed head.  So if your severed head was watching TV,
you learn and remember what it learned and remembers from the TV show, and don't forget stuff you did in your headless body, either.
If something special happens, like the bottom bloody stump area of your head getting burnt by fire or acid, then your head won't re-attach.
The same problem happens if your neck on your torso gets burnt or something.  Your skin is nearly immune to fire, but your inside flesh can
be burnt like that so it can't reattach severed parts or heal properly.  This is a weakness of your half-dragon anatomy.  Getting the flesh
ruined so it can't re-attach and heal throws a monkey wrench into getting your head's memories, meaning you have let it talk to you for a bit.
After being done with that, the best thing to do is to kill your head so you can re-grow a new one and throw away the old one you kill.
You have to do it this way because you can only have one head that's alive at a time, whether it is severed or connected.
Having your head connected is of course nice, as it gives you extra actions per combat turn, and many combat bonuses, etc.
"Okay \P[1], we should get outta here.  But we need to talk more, later."
"Not too much later though.  The bad guys aren't gonna sit around waiting when they find out what's going on."
There's no reason to put your head back on the fence.  It won't do any good.
Before you is a doorway, apparently leading to more of this funhouse of a hand-made mini-world of some sort.
"You guys really want to go in there?"
"There's not much else to do in this place.  Might as well."
"Well you've always been the 'Master Decision-Maker', and our leader, if there is one."
"It *DOES* look rather...  Um, plain and boring."
"Yeah, it's all bare, nothing in it, no furniture or anything.  Just like the Inn.  Talk about a rush job."
"What are in all these bins and crates?"
\P[3] gestures left and right around the room with his hand.
You peer inside some of the stuff.
"Stone, dirt, rocks, bricks, wood, cement, stuff sold in hardware stores, and other fun stuff.
Enough to build a bunch more rooms like these."
"Okay, we might as well find out what's down these hallways..."
Before you is a doorway, apparently leading to more of this funhouse of a hand-made mini-world of some sort.
